title: Keyboard shortcuts
subtitle: Only shortcuts that are actually wired are listed here.

goto.name: Go to
goto.explainer: A two-step sequence: press G, release, then type the letter. It stays quiet while you are typing in a field, and it expires after a second and a half.

global.name: Everywhere
global.explainer: A chord: both keys at once, on any screen. Only {{copilot}}'s shortcut also answers from inside a text field.

dossier.name: In an account file
dossier.explainer: A single key, on an account file. It stays quiet while you are typing in a field.

rafale.name: In burst mode
rafale.explainer: Single keys, in burst mode (one card at a time, full screen). They stay quiet while you are typing in a field.

rafale.primary: Approve, copy and open, or mark done

describe.laura: Opens {{copilot}} from anywhere — even mid-sentence in a field.
describe.sidebar: Collapses the sidebar down to its icons, and opens it again.
describe.escape: Closes the open panel or dialog, cancels what you were typing.
describe.global-search: Opens search across accounts, contacts, needs, consultants, assignments, actions and settings, from anywhere.
describe.goto-today: Opens the daily brief: what deserves your attention now.
describe.goto-accounts: Opens the list of your accounts.
describe.goto-projects: Opens your pipe and the needs attached to it.
describe.goto-actions: Opens the log of your actions.
describe.goto-pilotage: Opens steering: your figures and the axes behind them.
describe.dossier-search: Puts the cursor in the account file search: people, entities, signals, projects, needs, assignments, actions, proofs, history and sources, without knowing which section they live in.
describe.rafale-next: Moves to the next card of the deck.
describe.rafale-prev: Goes back to the previous card of the deck.
describe.rafale-edit: Opens the card draft so you can edit it before approving.
describe.rafale-primary: Does the main gesture of the card; never sends a message on its own.
describe.rafale-skip: Skips the card without handling it.
describe.rafale-help: Shows or hides the list of burst shortcuts.

page.subtitle: What they do, where they answer, and how they read on your keyboard.
page.needsKeyboard: These shortcuts need a physical keyboard. On a touch screen, everything they do stays reachable by hand, through the navigation.

customize.title: Changing them
customize.intro: Not possible yet — and rather than leave you guessing, here is exactly what is missing.

blockers.handler: Collapsing the sidebar is handled by a shared component that cannot read your settings. A key remapped here would show up without triggering anything.
blockers.reserved: Remapping a chord means knowing which ones your browser and your operating system have already taken. Without that list, we would cost you a shortcut you use a hundred times a day.
blockers.perDevice: Your interface settings are kept in this browser today, so on this machine. A shortcut remapped here would not exist on your other computer — and a gesture that changes from one machine to the next is never learnt.
